definitions.explanation_en: With an infinitive, it forms the near future: aller + infinitive.
Apprendre quelque chose means learn something; apprendre à quelqu'un means teach someone.
Also builds many compound tenses as an auxiliary.
Often appears in quelque chose, meaning something.
Comprendre que introduces a complete idea or clause.

definitions.english_gloss: to know; to be familiar with
definitions.explanation_en: Use for people, places, and things you are familiar with.
Expresses obligation or strong likelihood depending on context.
A high-frequency irregular verb used in many fixed expressions.
A common irregular verb with many everyday uses.
Parler de means to talk about; parler à means to speak to someone.
With ne, personne means nobody; without it, it means a person.
Usually followed by an infinitive to express ability or permission.
Its meaning changes naturally in common expressions and collocations.
Avoir raison means to be right.
Savoir concerns facts or learned ability; connaître concerns familiarity.
The intended meaning is determined by context: le temps passes; quel temps fait-il? asks about weather.
Travail is usually masculine and commonly used without an article in expressions.
Venir de + infinitive expresses the recent past.
Use the conditional je voudrais to make requests more polite.
Names identity, state, location, and serves as an auxiliary for several movement verbs.
Movement verbs such as aller commonly use être as their auxiliary; the past participle agrees with the subject.
definitions.explanation_zh: 像 aller 这样的移动动词在复合过去时中常用 être 作助动词；过去分词与主语保持性数一致。

definitions.explanation_en: A high-frequency expression: avoir besoin de + noun or infinitive.
definitions.explanation_zh: 常用表达：avoir besoin de + 名词或不定式。

definitions.explanation_en: A completed past action built with a present auxiliary and a past participle.
Aller in the present tense followed by an infinitive expresses a near or intended future.
Standard negation usually places ne before the verb and pas after it.
A reflexive pronoun refers back to the subject and forms part of the verb construction.
A conjunction such as que introduces a clause dependent on another clause.
